messages:
alex.s: Heads-up — noticed a p99 regression for Sundial-v2 after the tokenizer normalization change. Only shows up on long-context customers (~50k+ tokens). p95 up ~30%, p99 ~2.5x. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/longctx/sundial-v2

jordan: which route / model variant? dedicated or hosted? any correlation with KV cache miss rate?

alex.s: hosted, model=sundial-v2, variant=tokenizer-normalize-v2 (rolled 03/08). KV cache miss rate jumped from 4% to ~18% for long sessions. See quick logs below.

riley: can you paste a short repro? even a curl with a long prompt is fine.

alex.s: repro command I used:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"sundial-v2","input":"'"$(python -c 'print("X ".strip()*12000)')"'","max_tokens":256}'
```

(alternatively paste a 40k char lorem)

samira: logs snippet from inference node (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-08T14:22:11Z] request_id=req_7a9 kvcache_lookup=false tokens=48712 tokenizer_variant=normalize-v2 latency_ms=1200
[2026-03-08T14:22:11Z] request_id=req_7a9 kvcache_populated=false reason=token_split_expand
[2026-03-08T14:22:11Z] request_id=req_7a9 forward_pass_ms=980 kernel_launch_ms=150 overhead_ms=70
```

riley: "token_split_expand" looks suspicious — could be new subword merges producing many more subtokens so KV cache keys change. Did the tokenizer change introduce extra BPE merges or emit different EOS markers?

alex.s: yes, normalization adds NFKC + CJK compatibility mapping -> some inputs expand by ~1.2x tokens. But 2.5x p99 suggests additional fragmentation.

jordan: can we quantify token inflation per-customer sample? Also, any change in batching behavior for long sequences?

samira: ran quick sample diff: original tokenizer -> 48.7k tokens; normalize-v2 -> 62.1k tokens for same input. KV cache miss rate for that request was 92%.

ops-bot: alert: longctx-p99 spike detected (service:sundial-v2) at 2026-03-08T14:20:00Z; reroutes disabled.

alex.s: Immediate mitigation suggestions:
- rollback tokenizer variant to normalize-v1 for hosted traffic (canary)
- enable fallback routing to smaller-context variant (sundial-v2-shortctx) for sessions >40k tokens
- temporarily increase KV cache warmup window / persist prefix cache for long sessions

riley: quick mitigation applied: rolled back tokenizer variant on canary pool (canary id=can-42). Monitoring now.

deploy-bot: deploy: rollback-tokenizer normalize-v1 -> can-42 started at 2026-03-08T14:35:12Z by riley

jordan: was able to reproduce locally with your curl; p99 dropped back to baseline after rollback. Need follow-ups:
- postmortem of tokenizer normalization (why tokenized length increased so much)
- perf tests for long-context before boarding new tokenizer variants
- add regression test that compares token inflation and kvcache miss delta for +/-50k inputs

samira: created a ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3241 with repro steps, logs attached. Assigned to eng-ml.

alex.s: customer impact: three larger customers saw 2-3x request latency during the window; support already notified customers with temporary mitigation note.

jordan: next: eng-ml to provide a patch that preserves token alignment or emits compatibility tokens. Also product wants opt-out flag per-customer for tokenizer changes.

riley: will keep canary running for 2 hours and then schedule controlled rollout with perf gate. I'll post updates here. :thumbsup:
